subject: SIG questionnaire: cryptography & KMS scope clarification
messages:
From: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@veridianbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@veridianbank.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG questionnaire — cryptographic & KMS items

Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is Veridian's SIG-lite questionnaire with a focused section on cryptography and key management. For our internal review we need granular answers to the items below plus supporting artifacts where possible. Target turnaround: 2 weeks (EOD 2027-06-24).

Top asks we want to prioritize:
1) Key custody model across deployment modes (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) — who controls keys, and where are keys stored?
2) Key rotation evidence (timestamped rotation logs, KMS audit entries, and the process owner)
3) TLS cipher suites and termination points (load balancer vs host) — we need a short summary and a recent cipher scan output
4) Subprocessor list and any subprocessor-specific key handling (e.g., does a subprocessor ever hold plaintext or encryption keys)
5) Any technical controls that demonstrate separation between customer tenant data and platform service keys

Attachments we expect (stubs are fine): rotation logs, subprocessor.csv, TLS scan. Please point us to hosted links if there are size limits.

If you need to scope this narrower (e.g., only Dedicated), let me know — the broader we can cover the better for the procurement and security review.

Thanks,
Amanda Cole
Senior Security Engineer
Veridian Bank

---
Attachment: veridian_SIG_questions_cryptography.pdf (pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@veridianbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — cryptographic & KMS items

Amanda — thanks for the clear ask. We'll prepare the materials and clarify scope so we don't over/under deliver. Quick clarifying questions before we assemble artifacts: 

1) Scope: do you want answers for Hosted API + Dedicated + Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) or just the deployments you are evaluating (I believe the PO mentioned Dedicated)? If you confirm "all modes" we'll include short, mode-specific notes.
2) Rotation evidence: would a KMS rotation audit export (JSON entries with timestamps and principal IDs) plus a short narrative be sufficient, or do you need a notarized/3rd-party attestation?
3) TLS: do you require network-level scan output (e.g., testssl.sh results) or is a load-balancer config + recent scan sufficient?

Karthik — can you surface the latest key rotation audit for our production KMS (hosted) and a summary for Dedicated key options (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed) by Friday?
Jasmine — once Karthik drops the artifacts, I'll draft the SIG responses and upload to Veridian's portal; can you help with the portal submission and tracking?

We can also provide a short write-up on our routing/fallback policy (how requests are routed between regions/variants and the controls that prevent key exposure).

Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@veridianbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@veridianbank.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — cryptographic & KMS items

Thanks Irene — apologies for not being explicit. Confirming:
- Scope: Please include Hosted API and Dedicated. Private (customer-managed on-prem) only if you have a standard configuration or runbook to share — otherwise we can treat that as out-of-scope for now.
- Rotation evidence: we prefer the raw audit entries (timestamp + principal) for the last 12 months, plus a short narrative describing the guardrails/automation that perform rotation. A 3rd-party attestation is nice-to-have but not required at this stage.
- TLS: a recent testssl.sh output or equivalent external-facing scan is preferred (we run our own verification, but the scan helps triage differences).

Also: please include the current subprocessor list (CSV) and call out any subprocessor that has access to encryption keys or to customer data in plaintext.

Appreciate the fast turnaround. If you can get the KMS log export by Friday it will help us triage quickly.

Amanda

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — cryptographic & KMS items

Amanda — attaching the artifacts we discussed and summarizing below. Thanks for the clear priorities; we scoped to Hosted API + Dedicated only as requested.

Summary (high level):
- Key custody: Hosted API — Redwood-managed KMS (AWS KMS) by default; Dedicated — customer can opt for customer-managed keys (CMKs) in their cloud account or we can configure Redwood-owned but dedicated CMKs for contractual isolation. Private on-prem configurations are handled case-by-case and are out-of-scope for this packet.
- Rotation evidence: attached is a filtered export of rotation and key usage audit events for the last 12 months (kms-key-rotation-report-2027.pdf). The export includes timestamps, key IDs, and principal identities (service accounts). We also include a short narrative of our rotation automation and guardrails.
- TLS: attached is the latest external-facing cipher scan (tls-cipher-scan.txt) and a short note that our public API terminates TLS at our managed edge (load balancers) with TLS 1.2/1.3 configurations and modern cipher suites only. We also include host-level TLS config snippets for Dedicated instances where applicable.
- Subprocessors: subprocessor-list.csv attached. Column highlights indicate which subprocessors touch plaintext customer data; none of our listed subprocessors hold platform master keys.
- Separation controls: we included a brief architecture note describing KMS access boundaries, least-privilege IAM roles, and automated rotation keys that prevent operator access to plaintext keys.

Attachments included (stubs):
- kms-key-rotation-report-2027.pdf (pdf, sanitized export)
- subprocessor-list.csv (csv)
- tls-cipher-scan.txt (text)

Karthik — thanks for pulling the rotation export and the host config snippets.
Jasmine — please upload these to Veridian's shared intake portal and mark the submission as "SIG — cryptography packet". Follow up with Veridian procurement to confirm the portal record ID and let me know if they ask for anything further.

Next steps:
- I'll follow up with a compact write-up we can paste into the SIG fields (short answers + links to artifacts).
- If Veridian needs additional artifacts (e.g., longer log windows or HSM attestation letters), we'll coordinate next week.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
